Cui Jian Portrait

This black-and-white studio portrait presents Cui Jian, the influential Chinese rock musician born in 1961. His contemplative gaze and casual attire reflect the era when he transitioned from classical trumpet player to rock pioneer. The image’s simplicity underscores his role as a cultural icon who challenged musical norms in 1980s China.

Cui Jian Portrait

Cui Jian, often hailed as the father of Chinese rock, is captured here holding a trumpet, dressed in an olive-green jacket and a white cap adorned with a red star. His calm yet determined gaze reflects decades of dedication to authentic rock music, from his groundbreaking 1986 debut to his ongoing efforts to preserve the genre’s spirit.

Cui Jian’s "Keep Rocking" Livestream Concert

Cui Jian, often hailed as the "Father of Chinese Rock," returned to the stage with a three-hour vertical-screen livestream concert on WeChat Video Channel. Sporting his signature white cap embedded with a red star and a small beard, he opened with new material before revisiting classics such as "The Lonely Warrior" and "Flower House Girl." The concert poster featured evocative lines from his song "Egg Under the Red Flag," reflecting on the tension between hardness and vulnerability.
